newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Harmony bids for two mines.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Harmony bids for two mines.

text.p: South African mine Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it planned to bid for its Randgold stablemate mine Grootvlei and Grootvlei's neighbour Consolidated Modderfontein.
The bids value Grootvlei shares at 1,147 cents each and Cons Modder shares at 229 cents each.
Harmony said the move marked another stage in the firm's growth strategy and a further consolidation of gold mining in the East Rand basin.
Cons Modder shareholders will be offered six Harmony ordinary shares for every 100 Cons Modder Shares. The offer is subject to acceptance by shareholders holding at least 90 percent of the firm.
Grootvlei shareholders will get 30 Harmony shares for every 100 Grootvlei shares. Harmnony is also seeking to buy the Grootvlei management contract from Randgold.
Harmony said it is planning to increase the combined production volumes of Cons Modder and Grootvlei by 50 percent over the next thre years.

"The proposed transaction will broaden our asset base and our horizons and it will do so at a reasonable price which is well within Harmnony's budget," said Harmony managing director Bernard Swanepoel.

He added that the two neighbouring mines presented the firm with many synergies and cost-saving opportunities. Harmony is prepared to invest up to 65 million rand over the next four years to upgrade facilities and accelerate ore development at the two mines.
Taken together the two mines have 6.4 million ounces of resources of which 1.4 million ounces can be classified as reserves.
"The financial benefits of the proposed merger will enable them to improve the ratio between reserves and resources and give them greater flexibility in planning their operations," Harmony said.
The current Grootvlei management team would run both mines, Harmony added.
